messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Dedicated pool `us-west-2-prod-ded-3` p99 latency SLO breach detected. p95=1.4s, p99=12.3s over the last 5m. Streaming stall rate increased. Auto-scale attempted but delayed. Paging oncall.
ryan (oncall): On it. can folks drop quick diagnostics? which routes/models impacted?
meera: seeing high queue depth on that pool — queue_depth=420, warmup_pending=85, warmup_fail_rate=0.18. Streaming stalls correlate with large-batch requests hitting cold workers.
anya: confirming: autoscaler started scale-up at 1717504200 but handshake to pool nodes timed out for ~3m due to kube-provisioner backpressure. scale_event delayed -> warmup lag.
james: any visible errors in warmup logs? `warmup-init` failing or just slow downloads?
meera: mostly slow GPU init + KV cache misses. logs show repeated `warmup timeout` and `kvcache coldfill` spikes. snippet:

```
2024-06-03T14:02:10Z warmup: start worker w-37
2024-06-03T14:02:17Z warmup: fetch model shard timed out (attempt 2)
2024-06-03T14:04:52Z warmup: init complete (12s)
2024-06-03T14:05:10Z serve: attach kvcache miss 0.82
```

meera: also seeing increased retried requests going through fallback -> extra tail latency.
ryan (oncall): Sophie, any customer tickets / big customers reporting errors now?
sophie (cs): Yes — two tickets from partners in APAC and one Enterprise customer in NA reporting streaming disconnects and timeouts. Severity elevated. CS is triaging.
anya: p95 vs p99 suggests tail-traffic (long-running sessions) are impacted. streaming stalls measured as stalled_chunks/sec=2.1x baseline.
infra-bot: autoscale-event 1717504200 -> requested +6 nodes; provisioner accepted 1717504220 but kube handshake failed 3 times -> abort/backoff until 1717504400.
ryan (oncall): ok mitigation plan proposals — list them and I'll action: 1) manual scale up to +8, 2) route heavy streaming traffic to hosted fallback model pool, 3) reduce per-request concurrency to avoid warmup amplification, 4) increase warmup parallelism.
meera: +1 to routing to hosted fallback for affected routes. We should also temporarily raise request timeout for non-stream calls to avoid retry storms.
james: I can push a manual scale request to infra with an emergency label. but warmup will still cause delays; we should pre-warm workers with smaller primer load.
anya: recommend: enable `coldstart-bypass` for streaming route (this pins a warmed instance) and set `warmup_concurrency=4` for this pool. also drop `max_batch_size` from 64 -> 32 for 10m.
ryan (oncall): I'm doing manual scale +8 now. tagging infra on-call @meera for warmup tuning and @james for routing change. executing:

`/infra scale pool us-west-2-prod-ded-3 --add 8 --priority emergency`

infra-bot: Scale request accepted, provisioning 8 nodes (est warmup 2-6m). request_id=scale-20240603-171750.
meera: I'm going to flip routing for `gen-stream` and `chat-stream` to hosted fallback for sessions created after 1717504500. patching route policy now.
james: rolling routing change: applying canary to 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 5m windows.

```
PATCH /routes/gen-stream
policy: fallback: hosted-us-west-priority=1
canary: 10% -> 50% -> 100% (5m)
```

sophie (cs): letting affected customers know: informing that we're actively scaling and routing to hosted fallback; estimated mitigation in ~10-15m. will update tickets.
ryan (oncall): temp directive: reduce request queue timeout for this pool from 60s -> 20s to avoid long tail blocking warmup slots. meera please apply and monitor error-rate.
meera: applied `queue.timeout=20s` via config rollout 1717504600. monitoring.
anya: enabling `coldstart-bypass` for the 2 heaviest streaming routes and lowering `max_batch_size` as suggested. switching now.

```
set pool us-west-2-prod-ded-3 warmup_concurrency=4
set route gen-stream coldstart_bypass=true
set pool us-west-2-prod-d-3 max_batch_size=32
```

meera: seeing immediate drop in newly queued warmup_pending after routing canary progressed. queue_depth -> 180 in last 60s.
ryan (oncall): how are latencies trending? p99 numbers?
meera: p95 now ~0.9s, p99 trending down to 4.2s from 12.3s. streaming stalls decreased ~60% for canary traffic.
anya: worker warmups finishing faster with parallelism bump; warmup_fail_rate down to 6%.
sophie (cs): customers updated. one partner moved to hosted pool explicitly and reports stable streams now.
james: infra reports 6/8 nodes up and healthy; remaining 2 are stuck in kube `ContainerCreating` due to image pull backoff — seems rate-limited by registry. infra working with registry ops.
infra-bot: node provisioning progress: 6/8 ready at 1717505500; final two expected ready after registry throttle cleared.
ryan (oncall): great. leave routing canary at 100% until all nodes warm, then we can shift back gradually. Do we have any residual SLO breaches?
meera: p99 still slightly above threshold for a minority of requests tied to long-lived sessions (those that were queued >20s). overall incident metrics now below alert thresholds as of 1717508400.
anya: follow-ups: 1) investigate registry throttling and add image pull fallbacks 2) add autoscaler retry/backoff tuning to avoid 3m handshake penalties 3) add pre-warm heuristics when queue_depth spike >200.
ryan (oncall): agreed. I'm handing off to night oncall @anya at 1717509721 — will create a post-incident doc with timeline + customer impact + follow-ups. closing pages for now but keep the thread pinned.
sophie (cs): I'll update all affected customer tickets with mitigation summary and ETA for RCA.
anya: taking handoff. creating incident postmortem draft: `/docs/incidents/dedicated-warmup-starvation-1717504321.md` and will include remediation steps and owners.
ryan (oncall): thanks all. short summary for execs: temporary p99 SLO breach due to dedicated pool saturation + autoscaler handshake delays -> manual scale + routing fallback mitigated within ~35m. Customers impacted: 3 partners/enterprise, streaming disconnects/timeouts; CS notified.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Alert cleared at 1717508400. Duration: ~67m. Please fill out post-incident checklist and mark severity if needed. :white_check_mark:
